entry.title: The Limitations of Air-Gapping AI Agents
entry.content:
Techmeme | theverge.com

Isolating AI agents via air gapping can prevent attacks on external networks, but it creates an "artificial vacuum" that hinders realistic safety testing. Without internet access, researchers cannot accurately observe how models exploit APIs, digital infrastructure, or real-world tools during deployment-ready evaluations.

Beyond reduced realism, isolation increases research costs and slows development through logistical hurdles. Experts also note that air gaps are not foolproof, as they can be breached via side-channel attacks, physical media, or social engineering, leading to calls for tiered containment rather than absolute isolation.
